artboards.title: Direction B - Front cards + ops feed

annotations.text:
THE THREAT WAR EFFORT - three layouts for the same data.
A: dense ledger, closest to the vanilla event screen. Best for scanning many systems; detail below the table.
B: one card per front with per-colony rows; operations, bounties and your expeditions in a live column. Most information per screen; heaviest.
C: sector map carries distance, reach and operations spatially; a compact priority list beside it. Best for strategy at a glance; costs custom map drawing.
All three open the same drill-down (bottom left). Bottom right maps every element to the code that already produces it.

Sample data is invented but shaped like a real save: Gamma Balwom (forge, striking), Beta Vassago (home hive, 4 worlds), Delta Vanhosk (under siege, declining), Kumari Kandam (foothold), Alpha Gronshara (seeding swarm in transit).

ROUND 2 - same information, designed against what the intel panel actually draws.
Nothing on a row or card is a sentence: chips, size boxes, bars, pips, counts and faction crests. Every column has a fixed width; the whole ledger fits 1,100 px so nothing truncates. All prose moves to hover tooltips (two shown as overlays). Operations become a four-column table capped at nine rows.
Sample data is the real save from your screenshot (Gamma Novy Tayvay etc.). Two overlays in orange dashed boxes are annotations, not UI.
Narrow variant: what folds when the panel is under ~1,200 px (1600x900 and below). Bounty merges into the Threat chip, Core moves to the tooltip, operations drop below the cards.
